title: Rework presubmit/lint bootstrap, add presubmit heuristics and dependency timestamping
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: our presubmit pipeline has grown heavy — a single monolithic lint entrypoint pulls in language toolchains and full dependency installs which increases timer-to-feedback and CI cost. This PR splits bootstrapping duties, adds a lightweight presubmit heuristic router to reduce unnecessary expensive checks, and introduces a small metadata change to dependency bumps (dep timestamping) to make automated dependency churn more traceable. Motivation: speed up developer feedback loops, reduce CI minutes by ~25% on average, and make dep PRs easier to triage. What this PR does (single continuous description): - Split lint/test bootstrap: introduce language-specific entrypoints (scripts/lint-entrypoint-{py,ts,go}.sh) and a minimal shared bootstrap that only downloads the toolchain for the languages touched by the PR. The presubmit manifest now declares per-language bootstraps so CI jobs only install what they need. - Presubmit heuristics: add tools/ci/presubmit_router.go that inspects the changed paths and routes to a slim, fast lane for docs/infra/README-only changes, a medium lane for small SDK changes (typechecks + unit tests), and a heavy lane for runtime/serving changes. Heuristics are configurable via .github/presubmit-config.yaml. - Dependency timestamping: add tools/dep/timestamp_updater.py which appends a machine-readable timestamp and source tag to package bump commits authored by the automation bot. This helps downstream alerts and reduces noisy “unknown origin” churn in the dep dashboards. - Backwards compatible: default behavior is unchanged unless the presubmit-config is present in the repo or a repo-specific override exists. Migration notes and rollout strategy: feature-flagged behind ci.feature.split-boot, gradually enabled for active contributors and then org-wide. We ran a canary for three weeks in redwood-examples and SDK repos. Observed impact: median presubmit wall-clock dropped from 6m45s -> 4m50s (roughly 28% faster) and average CI-minute consumption reduced by ~21% across sampled runs. Checklist: - [x] introduce split entrypoint scripts - [x] implement presubmit router and config - [x] add timestamping util and integrate with dep-bot workflow - [x] docs updated (docs/ci/presubmit.md) - [x] e2e smoke runs in redwood-examples - [x] add tests for presubmit router heuristics Related: Linear ENG-8427 (presubmit fast lanes), ENG-8431 (dep metadata and dashboards). Related PRs: #1584102 (dep-bot: add metadata support), #1579023 (ci: minor workflow refactor).
commits_summary: 5 commits: split lint bootstraps and add per-language scripts; add presubmit router implementation + tests; add presubmit-config YAML and doc; dep timestamping tool + integration patch for dep-bot workflow; update CI workflows to call router and selective bootstraps.
reviews: Arjun Patel (review): Nice separation of concerns. Two requests: make the router config evaluate path globs before language heuristics (so docs-only PRs route even if a docs script touched a go file), and add a short-circuit in the bootstrap when TOOLCHAIN_LOCK is present to use cached toolchains.
Maya Chen (author reply): Good catches — reordered evaluation and added TOOLCHAIN_LOCK short-circuit in the 3rd commit. Also added a unit test covering the glob precedence case.
Liam O'Connor (review): Please ensure the timestamp format is RFC3339 and add a small consumer test in the dep dashboard parser. Also: confirm dep-bot workflow still signs commits correctly.
Maya Chen (author reply): Timestamp uses RFC3339 UTC; added parser test and validated dep-bot commit signing is unaffected (timestamp appended in commit message footer).
Sara Gupta (approval): Tests and docs look good. Observability changes (presubmit CI metrics) will require a follow-up dashboard PR but this is approved from the SRE side.
release_notes: Reduce presubmit latency by splitting language bootstraps and add presubmit heuristics to avoid running expensive checks on low-risk PRs. Add dep timestamping to dependency-bump commits for better traceability.
